title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 536-539 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): G is a linear algebraic group with a determinant-type character δ_G = det (essentially GL_2), and SG = ker det. ρ and σ are two automorphisms or twisting operations on G. M_{ρ,σ} is an algebraic group of 'systems' x. It carries a character χ: M_{ρ,σ} → G_m and a map Θ_G: M_{ρ,σ} → G, written U = Θ_G(x). B'_0 ⊂ G is a subgroup (Borel-like) whose elements are written u.

The previous page (538) proves an existence theorem. Take sections α, β, f of G with (det α)^2 = det β = det f = 1 (27). They arise from a system (x,u) via α = u a^{-1}, β = u b^{-1}, f = u U^{-1} (30) if and only if the 'loop relation' (31) holds: αρ(α)^{-1} = ε·βσ(β)^{-1}·(μ-term), for suitable ε in μ_n and μ in G_m. This condition involves only α and β, not f. In the case f = 1 (u = U) the pair (x,u) is unique. One gets a 1-1 correspondence between sections of the subobject M_{ρ,σ}[0] and pairs (α,β) satisfying the determinant conditions, (27) and the loop relation.

This page:
1. For that f = 1 correspondence, Grothendieck notes that the auxiliary group SM_{ρ,σ} is not needed.
2. For f arbitrary, the solutions (α,β,f) of (27) and (31) form an algebraic group. He calls its structure 'quite strange' and wants to revisit it geometrically, since it treats the three quantities α, β, f almost symmetrically.
3. To interpret this group he introduces SM_{ρ,σ}, to be isomorphic as a group to the common solutions of (27) and (31). It is defined (32) as the set of triples (x,u,f) with x in M_{ρ,σ}, u in B'_0, f in SG (or SL_2), subject to f·U = u with U := Θ_G(x).
4. Since f is determined by (x,u), and the only constraint det f = 1 means det U = det u (i.e. χ(x) = δ_G(u)), he gets (33): SM_{ρ,σ} embeds in M_{ρ,σ} × B'_0 as {(x,u) | χ(x) = δ_G(u)}.
5. The next page restates this as the fibre product (34): SM_{ρ,σ} ≅ M_{ρ,σ} ×_{G_m} B'_0, taken over χ and δ_G restricted to B'_0. Two extension structures follow: kernel L_0 = ker(δ|B'_0) over M_{ρ,σ}, and kernel M^+ = ker χ over B'_0. M_{ρ,σ}[0] then embeds via the graph x ↦ (x, Θ_G(x)).

In modern terms: a 'special' (determinant-one) version of a group, obtained as the fibre product of two groups over G_m along characters. This is the same mechanism as SL_n = GL_n ×_{G_m} {1}, or as forming G ×_{G_m} H. Its purpose is to linearise the parametrisation of solutions of the loop equation, so that those solutions become a group torsor or group.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The identification 'det f = 1 ⟺ χ(x) = δ_G(u)' tacitly uses det Θ_G(x) = χ(x), which is stated only on the next page.

Calling SM_{ρ,σ} isomorphic 'as groups' to the solution set of (27),(31) needs that set to carry a group law. This is asserted rather than shown here; on p. 539 the group law is in effect defined through the fibre product (34).

ideas.what: Defining a 'special' subgroup SM_{ρ,σ} as the fibre product M_{ρ,σ} ×_{G_m} B'_0 over two characters (χ and det)
ideas.modern_name: fibre product of group schemes over a torus along characters (cf. SL_n = ker det, G ×_{G_m} H constructions)
ideas.where_published: general fibre-product formalism in SGA 3; this specific group is not published

ideas.what: Parametrising the solutions (α,β,f) of the determinant conditions plus the loop relation (31) by pairs (x,u) of a system group and a Borel-type group
ideas.modern_name: parametrisation/torsor description of the solution set of a twisted (ρ,σ) cocycle-type equation
ideas.where_published: only in these unpublished notes (Longue Marche sequel, cote 140-3)

ideas.what: Remark that the group of triples (α,β,f) has a 'strange', quasi-symmetric structure in α, β, f, deserving a geometric interpretation
ideas.modern_name: none clear (a ternary-symmetric group structure on solution triples)

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags that the algebraic group of triples (α,β,f) solving (27),(31) has an odd, quasi-symmetric structure in the three variables. He wants to understand it geometrically, and the remark is left unpursued.
missed.quote: quelque peu étrange d'ailleurs (sur laquelle il me faudra revenir un jour plus (géométriquement ...))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor open thread. A geometric explanation of the threefold symmetry among α, β, f might relate to the S_3-symmetry of the three-punctured line underlying loop-type equations, but this is speculative. The fibre-product construction itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine technical step: it repackages a solution set as a fibre product of algebraic groups over G_m. Its only non-routine content is a brief, unpursued remark that the triple structure is strange and calls for a geometric interpretation.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: '(det α)^? = det β = 1 de (27)', not '(det α = det β = 1 et (27))'; it matches (27) of p. 538, where (det α)^2 = det β = 1.
'Mais revenons au cas f quelconque', not 'cas γ quelconque'.
'des triplets (α, β, f)', not '(α, β, γ)'; likewise 'les trois quantités α, β, f'.
'groupe ... quelque peu étrange' / 'de manière quasi symétrique' (reading uncertain).
In (32) the constraint reads roughly 'f U = u' (written like '∫U = f'u'), with U defined (‖déf) as Θ_G(x): capital U, not small u. The third entry is 'f dans SG' (possibly SL_2).
In (33) the condition is 'χ(x) = δ_G(u)' (with '‖(det u)' underneath), not 'γ(x) = ...(u)'; this agrees with (34) on the next page.
'il y a lieu d'introduire SM_{ρ,σ} — qui sera isomorphe (en groupes) à celui des solutions communes de (27) (31)'.
